phrases-20-118-119-neither-hungering-nor.title: Promise in the Garden: 'Neither to Hunger Nor Thirst Nor Be Struck by the Sun'
phrases-20-118-119-neither-hungering-nor.note: Surah 20:118–119 promises Adam in the Garden 'not to hunger there or go naked, nor to thirst there' or feel the sun's heat, matching the exact clause sequence of Isaiah 49:10 and Revelation 7:16 ('They will hunger no longer, nor thirst anymore').

discussion.view: Muslim commentators interpret these four paired clauses as God's direct assurance to Adam that the Garden provides complete shelter and sustenance.
discussion.reply: The Genesis Eden narrative contains no such fourfold formula; instead, the paired promise ('not hunger... nor thirst... nor shall the sun strike them') is a distinctive prophetic and apocalyptic formula from Isaiah 49:10 and Revelation 7:16 that Surah 20:118–119 retrojects into the address to Adam.

phrases-20-118-119-neither-hungering-nor.quranEn: [118] Surely it is yours not to hunger there or go naked, [119] nor to thirst there or be exposed to the sun.’

nor to thirst there or be exposed to the sun.’

sources.title: Isaiah (LXX / Septuagint)
sources.en: They shall not hunger, neither shall they thirst; neither shall the heat nor the sun strike them; but he that has mercy on them shall comfort [them], and by fountains of waters shall he lead them.
highlights: They shall not hunger, neither shall they thirst; neither shall the heat nor the sun strike them

sources.title: Book of Revelation (NASB)
sources.en: "They will hunger no longer, nor thirst anymore; nor will the sun beat down on them, nor any heat; for the Lamb in the center of the throne will be their shepherd, and will guide them to springs of the water of life; and God will wipe every tear from their eyes."
highlights: They will hunger no longer, nor thirst anymore; nor will the sun beat down on them, nor any heat
